entries.title: Lamentations 5:1
segments:
In the darkest days of adversity, when all around us is gloom and desolation, we ought still to maintain our confidence in God, and to seek his presence and salvation by humble confession and supplication, united with sincere repentance and obedience.  If we do this, we may rest assured that our present sorrows, and those of God's people, will end in joy and gladness, even as God, at the appointed time, turned again the captivity of the Jews and restored them to their own land. 
 
The darkest eras in the history of both churches and individuals, often prove to be the seed-time of a glorious future harvest of holiness and prosperity.

entries.title: Lamentations 5:6
segments:
Given the hand; yielded up ourselves. 
 
  Assyrians; here used for the Chaldeans, of whose empire Assyria was now a part.  The Jews were at this time partly in Egypt, and partly under the Chaldeans.
